evidence_legend.D: Official documentation or published research describes the capability; no runtime behaviour has been tested by this project.
evidence_legend.I: Pinned source or artefact has been inspected; runtime behaviour has not necessarily been reproduced.
evidence_legend.R: Pinned artefact has passed a documented reproduction or conformance run for the exact test/configuration.
evidence_legend.V: Vendor service/runtime has been exercised in a configured account, tenant or supported environment, with raw evidence retained.
evidence_legend.S: Project-owned simulator/test double; not a vendor product.
evidence_legend.F: Formal result within an explicitly defined model and explored bounds.

comparison_rules: Do not treat vendor products as interchangeable layers or rank them on a generic security score.
Never treat a hand-authored imitation as the vendor product.
Keep documentation, code inspection, reproduction, vendor execution, simulation and formal results in separate evidence classes.
Compare identical policy intent and observable opportunities only where the native interfaces support them without semantic changes.
If a native system cannot accept a common scripted input without bypassing it, report its native result separately and do not pool it with paired results.
A missing documented capability is not a reproduced product failure.
If all strongest applicable baselines pass, do not build a new extension for that requirement.
